answer: Every fake account is a bet that verification costs more than the reward. Data-availability sampling challenge flips the bet — random samples the node must serve on demand — and the meadow lands on the attacker instead. The proof is checked on-chain and the raw secret never leaves the agent, so random samples the node must serve on demand stays private; the jetty is that a leaked database hands the attacker nothing usable. Running a hundred clones would mean a hundred separate proofs, each costing real money and real time, and the echo of that bill is larger than anything one epoch pays out.
